prerequisites.text: A personal GitHub account or administrative access to a GitHub organization.
prerequisites.label: Sourced
prerequisites.quote: You can create and register an OAuth app under your personal account or under any organization you have administrative access to.

prerequisites.text: A publicly shareable homepage URL and authorization callback URL.
prerequisites.label: Sourced
prerequisites.quote: In "Homepage URL", type the full URL to your app's website.

setup_steps.text: In the upper-right corner of any page on GitHub, click your profile picture, then click Settings.
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: In the upper-right corner of any page on GitHub, click your profile picture, then click Settings.

setup_steps.text: In the left sidebar, click Developer settings.
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: In the left sidebar, click Developer settings.

setup_steps.text: In the left sidebar, click OAuth apps.
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: In the left sidebar, click OAuth apps.

setup_steps.text: Click New OAuth App (or 'Register a new application' if you have not created an app before).
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: Click New OAuth App. Note If you haven't created an app before, this button will say, Register a new application.

setup_steps.text: In 'Application name', enter the name of your app (using only public information).
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: In "Application name", type the name of your app.

setup_steps.text: In 'Homepage URL', enter the full website URL for your app.
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: In "Homepage URL", type the full URL to your app's website.

setup_steps.text: Optionally, in 'Application description', enter a description visible to users.
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: Optionally, in "Application description", type a description of your app that users will see.

setup_steps.text: In 'Authorization callback URL', type your app's callback URL (up to 10 URLs supported).
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: In "Authorization callback URL", type the callback URL of your app. You can enter up to 10 callback URLs.

setup_steps.text: If using device flow, check 'Enable Device Flow'.
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: If your OAuth app will use the device flow to identify and authorize users, click Enable Device Flow.

setup_steps.text: Configure 'Expire user access tokens' (enabled by default; uncheck only if code lacks expiring token support).
setup_steps.label: Sourced
setup_steps.quote: Expire user access tokens is enabled by default. If your app's authentication code hasn't been updated to support short-lived tokens, uncheck the box

setup_steps.text: Click Register application to finish creating the OAuth app.
setup_steps.label: Sourced

scopes.text: repo: Grants full access to public and private repositories and organization-owned resources.
scopes.label: Sourced
scopes.quote: Grants full access to public and private repositories including read and write access to code, commit statuses, repository invitations, collaborators, deployment statuses, and repository webhooks.

scopes.text: public_repo: Limits access to public repositories only, including code, issues, statuses, and starring.
scopes.label: Sourced
scopes.quote: Limits access to public repositories. That includes read/write access to code, commit statuses, repository projects, collaborators, and deployment statuses for public repositories and organizations.

scopes.text: user: Grants read/write access to profile information, including user:email and user:follow.
scopes.label: Sourced
scopes.quote: Grants read/write access to profile info only. Note that this scope includes user:email and user:follow.

scopes.text: read:user / user:email: Grants read-only access to profile data or email addresses without write permissions.
scopes.label: Sourced
scopes.quote: Grants access to read a user's profile data.

scopes.text: admin:org: Grants full management of an organization, including teams, projects, and memberships.
scopes.label: Sourced
scopes.quote: Fully manage the organization and its teams, projects, and memberships.

scopes.text: offline_access: Requests an expiring access token and a refresh token even if not configured globally.
scopes.label: Sourced
scopes.quote: Requests an expiring access token and a refresh token, even if your OAuth app is not configured to use expiring tokens.

limits_before_approval.text: A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps.
limits_before_approval.label: Sourced
limits_before_approval.quote: A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps.

limits_before_approval.text: OAuth apps can register a maximum of 10 callback URLs.
limits_before_approval.label: Sourced
limits_before_approval.quote: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs. To add additional callback URLs, click Add callback URL.

limits_before_approval.text: Users can edit or reduce token scopes during authorization or after the flow is completed.
limits_before_approval.label: Sourced
limits_before_approval.quote: However, users can edit their scopes, effectively granting your application less access than you originally requested. Also, users can edit token scopes after the

approval_process.text: Standard OAuth apps do not require review or approval by GitHub before use.
approval_process.label: Inferred
approval_process.note: Page 2 describes the complete registration flow without any review stage before credentials can be used.

approval_process.text: If listing on GitHub Marketplace with paid plans or a badge, your organization must complete publisher verification.
approval_process.label: Sourced
approval_process.quote: To offer paid plans for your app or to include a marketplace badge in your app listing, you must complete the publisher verification process

approval_process.text: Publisher verification requires submitting profile info, enabling org-wide 2FA, and verifying an organization domain.
approval_process.label: Sourced
approval_process.quote: Publisher verification ensures that GitHub has a way to contact you, that you've enabled two-factor authentication for your organization, and that your organization's domain

likely_blockers.text: OAuth services cannot be used as the sole identity provider for an application.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.quote: Such Account Authorization Services are not intended to be used as the sole identity provider for your application or service.

likely_blockers.text: Suspension if presenting the app or login page in a manner that suggests GitHub sponsorship or endorsement.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.quote: presents itself or its login page in a manner that suggests sponsorship, endorsement, or affiliation with GitHub;

likely_blockers.text: Suspension if performing undocumented actions on behalf of the user, such as starring repositories without explicit disclosure.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.quote: misrepresents or obscures what it does (for example, if an application takes any actions, like starring repositories, on behalf of a user without this

likely_blockers.text: Offering paid plans in GitHub Marketplace requires organization ownership, 2FA, and a verified domain.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.quote: To offer paid plans for your app, the app must be owned by an organization and you must have owner permissions in the organization.

you_must_do: Sign in to your GitHub account and navigate to Developer settings.
Fill out and submit the OAuth App registration form.
Store and manage the generated client ID and client secret securely.
Configure organization 2FA and verify domain if requesting Marketplace publisher verification.
